name: Strahan
objection: Much of what visitors do is cruises and the railway (vehicles) and Hogarth Falls is its own spot; but the waterfront and harbour town itself is a second-tier harbour-town stop, and the guides give it its own page.

name: Ocean Beach
objection: Wild surf beach with dangerous swimming; one counted source only, but a clear scenic stop

name: Hogarth Falls
objection: Small cascade; one source; the walk is the draw. Judged with People's Park folded in

name: Water Tower Hill Lookout
objection: Short roadside-style view, one source; case for: free and named by a guide

name: Cape Sorell Lighthouse
objection: Exterior-only, remote (boat/4WD); for: a named landmark in the guide's See list

name: Sarah Island
objection: Only reachable by cruise, so the visit is bundled in an operator tour; the place still qualifies

name: Strahan Wharf Centre
objection: Could be a visitor centre exhibit rather than a museum; verify it still operates

name: Gordon River
objection: A river is a long feature reached only via operator cruises; place pin at the cruise destination (Heritage Landing)

name: West Coast Wilderness Railway
objection: Case for: heritage rack railway with no single destination (the journey is the draw), 2 sources; against: an operator ticket and the places at its ends are the spots

name: Franklin River Nature Trail
objection: Roadside 20-30 min walk; for: DOC walk beside the Franklin River

name: Nelson Falls
objection: About 20 minutes return, a roadside walk on the Lyell Highway, could be a part of the park spot; but it is a named Great Short Walk with three counted sources, a second-tier stop.

name: Donaghys Hill Lookout
objection: Minor lookout on the highway; similar category to Nelson Falls, but a different walk

name: Frenchmans Cap Track
objection: One counted source; hard, exposed walk; but a clear draw

name: Lake Rhona Trail
objection: Long track to a lake, with little visitor detail

name: Franklin River
objection: Visited only by 8-9 day rafting expeditions; pin at the Lyell Highway crossing

name: King River
objection: One tourism-board mention, no visitor listing for a site

name: Lake Margaret
objection: Tour-only, one source; case for: a distinctive heritage place

name: Lake Burbury
objection: Fishing/lodge-based; little to do for 30 minutes otherwise

name: Lake St Clair
objection: Part of the national park and Overland Track spots; may be a near-duplicate if the park is itself a spot. Answer: the lake and its Cynthia Bay hub (cruise, short walks, visitor centre) is a distinct stop reached from the Lyell Highway; page views of 63k are polluted by Michigan so do not use them as evidence.

name: Echo Point
objection: Part of the Lake St Clair area; not a roadside outlook, a 3-7 hour circuit

name: Mount Rufus
objection: Another Great Short Walk of the same area; distinct but second-tier

name: Shadow Lake
objection: Same tier as Mount Rufus; little detail

name: Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Walk (Lake St Clair)
objection: Very minor, and part of Lake St Clair

name: Overland Track
objection: Overlaps the national park spot and Lake St Clair (the end point); but a named walk is a distinct draw and the pin goes mid-route. Booking and fees apply, not an objection to inclusion.

name: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
objection: Large park containing other kept spots; as a spot it overlaps them

name: Mount Ossa
objection: Remote multi-day side trip; sits in the north-west region too (flag duplicate)

name: The Wall in the Wilderness
objection: Single source and a 1-hour visit; but a clear draw

name: Iron Blow Lookout
objection: Brief roadside stop

name: Spion Kopf Lookout
objection: Short stop

name: Queenstown
objection: The Railway starts here and the town is a transit stop on the Lyell Highway; but the town has several open attractions of its own, so it passes as a town with its own draws.

name: The Galley Museum
objection: Small local-history museum, one source

name: Bradshaw's Sawmill
objection: Working business, so access varies

name: Zeehan
objection: Only one listed See item and a small town; but a one-street heritage mining town with an open museum fills half an hour to an hour, and is a second-tier town stop.

name: West Coast Heritage Centre
objection: One source, a small museum

name: Rosebery
objection: Town as base with services; for: the surviving mining community

name: Montezuma Falls
objection: One source; long walk

name: Stitt Falls
objection: Minor falls beside the Montezuma draw

name: Tullah
objection: Case against: a town is a spot only if the town is a draw, and its draws are the dam and a weekend-only railway, which are better as their own spots; case for: a few things to do and two counted sources. Judge Mackintosh Dam and Wee Georgie Wood Railway separately.

name: Mackintosh Dam
objection: Short roadside photo stop

name: Wee Georgie Wood Steam Railway
objection: A vehicle ride with a loop; weekends only; one source

name: Southwest National Park
objection: Mostly wilderness with limited access; park-level, destination-scale

name: Gordon Dam
objection: Single listing without text; but famous

name: Red Knoll Lookout
objection: Could be the lake's viewpoint; one source

name: Lake Pedder
objection: One source; mainly viewed from lookouts

name: Melaleuca
objection: Reachable only by plane or multi-day walk

name: Port Davey
objection: Remote; access only by boat or flight

name: South Coast Track
objection: One source; remote logistics

name: Cockle Creek
objection: Small settlement; part of the Huon region, mostly outside this region's west coast

name: Arthur-Pieman Conservation Area
objection: Large area; Edge of the World is its pin draw

name: Edge of the World
objection: A coastal viewpoint; part of the conservation area but a named stop

name: Arthur River
objection: Town wrapper near its attraction; for: the field centre and river cruises (not sourced)

name: Balfour
objection: Mostly visited on a tour, remote

name: Sandy Cape Beach
objection: Cold windy beach, hard access

name: Corinna
objection: Case for: historic Huon pine settlement, Pieman River cruise and a base for the Tarkine. Against: its draw is access to the Tarkine (the ferry is a vehicle), one real source, visit mostly a stopover; a town is a spot only if it is a draw itself.

name: Takayna / Tarkine
objection: Region-scale; duplicate of the north-west pass
